newsitem.title: NORWAY: Amoco gains shares in Ula,Gyda N.Sea fields.
newsitem.headline: Amoco gains shares in Ula,Gyda N.Sea fields.

text.p: Amoco Norway has gained equity production stakes in the North Sea Ula and Gyda oilfields by taking over Norwegian group Pelican AS, the company said on Thursday.

Pelican owns four percent in the British Petroleum Co Plc operated Gyda field and five percent in Ula. It also holds interests in exploration licences on the Danish continental shelf, close to Amoco's Valhall field.
No price was available for the deal.
Amoco spokesman Sveinung Sletten said the acquisition fitted the company's three-legged growth strategy in the region.

"Our strategy for growth includes maximising asset value in the Valhall region, exploration and acquisitions and divestments to optimise our portfolio. This acquisition fits into two of the three strategies," Sletten said.
Amoco is operator of the Valhall and Hod oilfields on the Norwegian continental shelf.

Pelican was established in 1971 and was owned by Selvaag Invest AS (38.2 percent), Norsk Hydro Produksjon AS (35.8 percent), Belships Company Ltd Skibs AS (10.4 percent), Actinor Olje AS (10.2 percent) and Kvaerner Rosenberg AS (5.4 percent).
